newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot, Continental begin code-sharing in April.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot, Continental begin code-sharing in April.

text.p: Russian flag carrier Aeroflot and Continental Airlines of the United States will begin a code-sharing programme from April, both companies said on Friday.
Valeri Okulov, Aeroflot acting chief executive, said the code-sharing deal would begin with joint ticket sales.
"We hope the programme will be profitable for both airlines," he said.
Berry Saimon, senior vice-president for Continental, told Reuters code-sharing flights may begin in September.
In January, both carriers signed a five-year code-sharing deal to operate Moscow-New York flights and coordinate their schedules, reservations and tariffs.

According to the agreement, Aeroflot and Continental would jointly operate a new daily flight between Moscow and New York's Newark airport as a hub to reach the 157 other U.S. cities to which Continental flies. A Continental DC-10-30 aircraft will fly on the route.

The deal means Russian passengers can buy tickets in Moscow for flights to these destinations just as U.S. passengers can fly from the United States to Russian and ex-Soviet destinations Aeroflot serves.
Aeroflot would continue to operate three flights a week from Moscow's Sheremetyevo to New York's Kennedy Airport operating a Boeing 767 jet.
"We also plan to cooperate with Continental on technical servicing, marketing and advertising," Okulov said.
Aeroflot plans to join Continental's frequent-flier programme soon.
